title: Polarized formal schemes over an adically complete Noetherian ring algebraize
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and assume that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X_n\to S_n$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with transition morphisms $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ over $S_n\to S_{n+1}$ such that $X_n\cong X_{n+1}\times_{S_{n+1}}S_n$ via $i_n$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose that $X_1\to S_1$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For every $n$ let $L_n$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\varphi_n:i_n^*L_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n$ be an isomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume that $L_1$ is ample on $X_1$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there exist a proper morphism $Y\to S$, an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $L$, isomorphisms $a_n:X_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_SS_n$ of schemes over $S_n$, and isomorphisms $b_n:L|_{X_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n$, compatible with $i_n$ and $\varphi_n$: compatibility of $a_n$ means that $a_{n+1}\circ i_n$ is the composite of $a_n$ with the closed immersion $Y\times_SS_n\to Y\times_SS_{n+1}$ induced by $S_n\to S_{n+1}$. Here $L|_{X_n}$ is pullback along $X_n\xrightarrow{a_n}Y\times_SS_n\to Y$, and compatibility of $b_n$ means $b_n=\varphi_n\circ i_n^*b_{n+1}$ under the canonical pullback identifications. Moreover $Y\to S$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]: there are $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_A$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 089A, theorem-algebraization; the finite-projective-space embedding is the construction in its proof, ending with lemma-algebraize-formal-closed-subscheme (Tag 0899).

proof.text: For $m<n$, compose the given cartesian squares to identify $X_m$ with the closed subscheme of $X_n$ cut out by $I^m\mathcal O_{X_n}$. This uses the affine quotient description of a closed immersion and base change. Its ideal is nilpotent, so all levels have the same underlying space and residue fields. For properness reflection substitute the ring $A/I^n$, ideal $J=I/I^n$, exponent $N=n$, and morphism $X_n\to S_n$. Here $J^n=0$ and its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}((A/I^n)/J)=S_1$ is $X_1\to S_1$ by the cartesian identifications. The reverse implication of the cited node therefore makes $X_n\to S_n$ proper; it assumes no prior finite type or flatness. Every $A/I^n$ is Noetherian: ideals lift to ideals of $A$, whose finite generating sets descend. Hence every $X_n$ is Noetherian.

Put $F_0=\mathcal O_{X_1}$ and, for $r\ge1$, put $F_r=\ker(\mathcal O_{X_{r+1}}\to\mathcal O_{X_r})=I^r\mathcal O_{X_{r+1}}$. All are sheaves on the common underlying space. For $m>r$, the quotient $I^r\mathcal O_{X_m}/I^{r+1}\mathcal O_{X_m}$ is canonically $F_r$, since $\mathcal O_{X_{r+1}}=\mathcal O_{X_m}/I^{r+1}\mathcal O_{X_m}$. Multiplication in any level $m>r+s$ therefore induces $F_r\otimes F_s\to F_{r+s}$, independent of $m$. Let $B=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}I^r/I^{r+1}$. A finite set of generators $a_i$ of $I$ gives degree-one generators $\bar a_i$ of $B$ over $A/I$: monomials generate every ideal power. Thus $B$ is a finite type graded algebra. The action maps give a surjection $(X_1\to S_1)^*\widetilde B\to\bigoplus_rF_r$, since every local section of $I^r\mathcal O$ is a sum of scalar ideal generators times local coefficients. The kernel ideals and their quotients are quasi-coherent, so $\bigoplus_rF_r$ is a finite type graded quasi-coherent module over this pulled-back algebra (generated by $1$ in degree zero).

source.place: Tag 089A, first two paragraphs: associated graded algebra

proof.text: Apply graded Serre vanishing on the proper scheme $X_1$ over the Noetherian ring $A/I$, to $B$, $\bigoplus_rF_r$ and the ample line $L_1$. Choose $d_0$ so its positive cohomology vanishes after twisting by every $d\ge d_0$. Each $F_r$ is a graded direct summand, so its $H^1$ is a retract of this zero group. Hence $H^1(X_1,F_r\otimes L_1^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $r$ and every $d\ge d_0$, with one bound independent of $r$.

Apply the relative-ampleness affine-cover criterion to $h:X_1\to S_1$, $N=L_1$, and the single affine open $U=S_1$. Properness makes $h$ quasi-compact, and $h^{-1}(U)=X_1$, where $L_1$ is ample by hypothesis. Thus $L_1|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq S_1$, so $L_1$ is $h$-ample. The morphism $h$ is also of finite type and its affine target $S_1$ is quasi-compact. The common-very-ample-power theorem therefore gives an integer $d_1$ such that $L_1^{\otimes d}$ is relatively very ample for every $d\ge d_1$. Choose $d\ge\max(1,d_0,d_1)$. The finite-coordinate-sections theorem over $S_1$ gives finitely many generating sections $s_{0,1},\ldots,s_{N,1}$ of $L_1^{\otimes d}$, an immersion $\psi_1:X_1\to\mathbf P^N_{S_1}$, and its quotient-compatible identification $\psi_1^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_1^{\otimes d}$. Projective space is proper, hence separated over $S_1$. Properness of $X_1\to S_1$ then makes $\psi_1$ proper by the proper-to-separated theorem. A proper immersion is closed, so $\psi_1$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 089A, second paragraph: choice of projective embedding

proof.text: Tensor $0\to F_r\to\mathcal O_{X_{r+1}}\to\mathcal O_{X_r}\to0$ by $L_{r+1}^{\otimes d}$. This is exact: on an open trivializing the line it is the original sequence. The prescribed $\varphi_r$ identify the quotient with $L_r^{\otimes d}$ and the kernel with the pushforward of $F_r\otimes L_1^{\otimes d}$, since $IF_r=0$. The module $F_r\otimes L_1^{\otimes d}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type on the Noetherian scheme $X_1$, hence coherent by the Noetherian coherence criterion. Closed-immersion cohomology identifies its $H^1$ with the zero group of step 3. The long exact sequence for global sections therefore makes $\Gamma(X_{r+1},L_{r+1}^{\otimes d})\to\Gamma(X_r,L_r^{\otimes d})$ surjective. Starting at the sections of step 4, lift the finite tuple at each successive level. This constructs $s_{i,r+1}$ with $\varphi_r^{\otimes d}(i_r^*s_{i,r+1})=s_{i,r}$.

source.place: Tag 089A, third paragraph: exact sequence and lifting sections

proof.text: At every point $x$ of $X_r$, the lifted sections have the same residue-field values as their generating tuple on $X_1$: by the fibre formula $(e^*\mathcal L)(x)=\mathcal L(e(x))\otimes\kappa(x)$, $(e^*s)(x)=s(e(x))\otimes1$ for the nilpotent closed immersion $e:X_1\to X_r$, a homeomorphism with $\kappa(x)=\kappa(e(x))$, applied to $e^*s_{i,r}\cong s_{i,1}$. They generate $L_r^{\otimes d}$ by the fibre criterion. The projective-space functor of points thus gives $\psi_r:X_r\to P_r=\mathbf P^N_{S_r}$ with its section-normalized identification $\psi_r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_r^{\otimes d}$. Its pullback compatibility gives $\psi_{r+1}i_r=\iota_r\psi_r$, because the associated pairs are identified by $\varphi_r^{\otimes d}$. The resulting squares are cartesian: $P_r=P_{r+1}\times_{S_{r+1}}S_r$, and pulling back $\psi_{r+1}$ gives precisely $X_{r+1}\times_{S_{r+1}}S_r=X_r$.

source.place: Tag 089A, last paragraph: compatible projective-space maps

proof.text: Base change of $\psi_r$ to the finite order thickening $P_1\subset P_r$ is $\psi_1$. A closed immersion is finite, and finite-morphism reflection across a finite order thickening therefore makes every $\psi_r$ finite. Apply finite formal-scheme algebraization to the fixed ambient $P=\mathbf P^N_A$ and the cartesian squares of step 6 (shifting its indices by one). The ambient scheme is proper over $S$, hence separated and finite type. We obtain a finite morphism $j:Y\to P$, a proper morphism $Y\to S$, and compatible isomorphisms $a_r:X_r\cong Y\times_SS_r$ over $P_r$.

source.place: Tag 089A, final paragraph; Tag 09ZT, lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper, expanding the fixed-ambient argument of Tag 0899

proof.text: The morphism $j$ is closed, not merely finite. Both $P$ and $Y$ are Noetherian since they are proper over the Noetherian affine base. Finite pushforward makes $E=j_*\mathcal O_Y$ coherent, and the coherent cokernel theorem makes $Q=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_P\to E)$ coherent. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P$, write its finite inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Reduction of $E$ modulo $I^r$ is the module $C/I^rC$, so it is the direct image of $\mathcal O_{X_r}$ under $\psi_r$. Right exactness of tensor (quotienting a presentation) identifies $Q/I^rQ$ with the cokernel of the reduced algebra map. This map is surjective: $\psi_r$ is a closed immersion by the following two-line calculation. The finite algebra map on any affine open of $P_r$ is surjective modulo the nilpotent ideal $J$ defining $P_1$; its module cokernel $V$ satisfies $V=JV=J^rV=0$. Thus all restrictions of $Q$ vanish. Every coherent module on proper $P$ has proper support; Grothendieck-existence faithfulness then sends $1_Q$ to zero at every level, hence $1_Q=0$ and $Q=0$. Thus $\mathcal O_P\to j_*\mathcal O_Y$ is a surjective map of quasi-coherent algebras; its image on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the image of $R\to C$, so $R\to C$ is surjective. Since $j$ is finite and hence affine, the affine surjective-ring-map criterion proves $j$ a closed immersion. Together with properness of $Y$ this proves the required projectivity.

source.place: Tag 0899, lemma-algebraize-formal-closed-subscheme, cokernel argument; Tag 09ZT for the finite algebraization; Tag 09ZW(8) for finite reflection

proof.text: Use $a_r$ to view $(L_r,\varphi_r)$ as coherent modules on the thickenings of $Y$. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian by step 8. They are coherent because they are locally free of rank one on Noetherian schemes. Apply Grothendieck existence (with index shifted from $r\ge1$ to $r-1\ge0$) to obtain a coherent module $M$ on $Y$ and compatible isomorphisms $b_r:M|_{X_r}\cong L_r$. Apply it also to the compatible dual lines $L_r^\vee$ to obtain $D$ with compatible dual identifications. The restriction comparisons for tensor products identify $(M\otimes D)|_{X_r}$ with $L_r\otimes L_r^\vee\cong\mathcal O_{X_r}$. The module $M\otimes D$ is coherent: tensor preserves quasi-coherence, and finite local generating sets tensor to a finite generating set; apply the Noetherian coherence criterion. All coherent modules on the proper scheme $Y$ have closed support, proper by closed-subset permanence. Full faithfulness of existence lifts these compatible evaluation isomorphisms and their inverses, and faithfulness makes their composites identities. Thus $M\otimes D\cong\mathcal O_Y$, so $M$ is invertible. Put $L=M$.

source.place: Tag 089A, final sentence expanded using Tags 088E/088F; recovery of the original polarization

proof.text: Put $H=j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_A}(1)$, ample by the projective-ample theorem. The section-normalized identifications of step 6 and the fact that $a_r$ is over $P_r$ give isomorphisms $H|_{X_r}\cong L_r^{\otimes d}$ compatible with restriction. The $b_r^{\otimes d}$ identify the same system with $L^{\otimes d}|_{X_r}$. Full faithfulness of Grothendieck existence lifts the resulting compatible isomorphisms and inverses to $H\cong L^{\otimes d}$. Hence $L$ is ample directly from its definition: any affine nonvanishing locus $Y_s$ of a section of $H^{\otimes k}$ is the same locus for the transported section of $L^{\otimes dk}$, with $dk>0$. Quasi-compactness is unchanged. Finally the compatibility equations for the $a_r$ are those of the algebraized closed-subscheme system, and those for the $b_r$ are exactly the equations supplied by Grothendieck existence. They are the two equations in the item, including the specified $\varphi_r$.
